title: Context inventory and budgets
statement: The workflow must provide a repeatable context inventory for Cartographer agent sessions that measures root AGENTS.md, child AGENTS.md files such as skills/AGENTS.md, active skill descriptions, high-use SKILL.md bodies, compaction summaries, state-resume payloads, and active tool/schema exposure.

title: Inventory reports top bloat sources
Changed files report before/after budget deltas
Inventory includes core AGENTS.md files, skills, compaction, resume, and tool-schema sources
Budget thresholds are documented for each context source family
Compact workflow skill kernels
statement: High-use Cartographer workflow skills must be split into compact SKILL.md kernels plus one-level on-demand references while preserving activation criteria, critical safety rules, execution loop, exact required wrapper sequence, stop conditions, and reference pointers.

title: Implement activates with compact resume-safe kernel
Low-frequency details load from named references on demand
Implement, plan, and proposal have explicit size budgets
References remain one level deep from SKILL.md
Safety and validation rules remain reachable after splitting
AGENTS.md hierarchy budget and locality
statement: Root and child AGENTS.md files must be audited for context locality, duplication, lint/readability, and durable-rule ownership so root AGENTS.md carries only project-wide rules and subtree rules live in narrower child AGENTS.md files.

title: Non-skills work receives slim root context
Skills work receives compact lint-clean child AGENTS.md context
Root and child AGENTS.md measured before and after relocation
skills/AGENTS.md line-length and duplicate-rule warnings are resolved or justified
Parent/child instruction ownership stays current
State-aware compaction and resume payloads
statement: Cartographer implementation resume must be driven by compact state, receipt, and context-pack summaries rather than historical narrative or full skill reinjection, prioritizing topic, phase, next action, working set, validation receipts, blockers, and critical rules.

title: Post-compaction turn resumes from state without full skill reload by default
Repeated compactions remain within a fixed summary budget
Resume summary has fixed target size and truncation/reference metadata
State transition tooling emits compact next action and guardrails
Raw transcript content is not copied into durable artifacts
Active tool/schema context control
statement: Cartographer must audit wrapper and extension tools for schema/prompt overhead and define an approach for reducing active tool context through phase-scoped profiles, consolidated tools, shorter schemas/snippets, or deferred discovery.

title: Proposal and design phases avoid implementation-only tool overhead
Implementation phase avoids proposal-only tool overhead
Tool inventory reports active count and estimated schema cost by phase
Design compares phase-scoped tools, schema compaction, consolidation, and deferred discovery
Tool reductions preserve auditability and mutation guardrails
Behavior-preserving migration and validation
statement: The context-reduction work must proceed through measurable phases, validating after each migration that proposal, requirements, design, plan, and implement workflows still expose required safety rules, wrapper calls, validations, and human gates.

title: Skill split preserves mandatory workflow sequence
Rule moved into tooling is proven by deterministic validation
Plan phases include baseline, split, validate, compaction, tool-schema, and regression work
Every removed rule has a documented new home or duplicate-deletion rationale
ADR finalization follows validated design choices
